Indian Standard
GRADING FOR SESAME SEEDS FOR OIL MILLING

o.

FO RE WO R D

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 21 October 1967, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilseeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council and the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Sesame seeds, commonly known as TIL, are obtained from the plant Sesamum indicum Linn. Syn. S. orientale Linn. which is cultivated in most of; the parts of India. These are of three types depending on the colour of the seeds, namely, white, brown and black. 0.3 Formulation of this standard has been taken up in order to meet the need felt for precise and acceptable methods for grading of oilseeds produced and marketed in the country. This standard is based on the trade practices followed in the country in respect of the types and grades. Sesame seeds are generally intended for oil milling; the better grades are, however, suitable for use in the preparation of sweets and confectionery. The oil obtained from these seeds is covered in IS: 547.1963� and IS: 4220E-1967t. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is compiled with. the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2..1960t. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the methods of grading and the requirements for sesame seeds for oil milling, along with the relevant methods of sampling and test.

2. TERMINOLOGY
2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 3579-1966� shall apply.
�Specification for sesame oil ( reoised ), ( Since reviled ). j Specificarion for solvent extracted sesame oil. (Since superseded by IS: 547 ). :Rules for rounding off numerical values ( ,1fIisH). �Methods of test for oilseeds.

3

IS I f429 .1967 3. TYPES
3.1 Sesame seeds grown in India shall be grouped into the following three types, based on the colour of their testa (outer coating). These are sold either as such or in mixtures.

3.1.1 Whit, Seeds - The colour of the testa of these seeds ranges from cream to white. These are grown in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Punjab and Andhra Pradesh. Another type of white seeds with distinctive characteristics of the oil is also grown in some areas of Assam, West Bengal and Tripura.
3.1.2 Brown Seeds - The colour of the testa of the seed ranges from light-brown to dark-brown. These are grown in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Punjab and Andhra Pradesh. 3.1.3 Black Seeds - The colour of the testa of the seed ranges from dark-brown to black. These are grown in Orissa, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.

4. GRADES
4.1 The sesame seeds of all the three types or their mixtures shall be graded as follows d~~ndi~g on the requirements prescribed in 5: a) Grade 1, b) Grade 2, and c) Grade 3.

5. REQ,UIREMENTS
5.1 Sesame seeds of the three types or their mixtures shall be graded in accordance with the physical and chemical requirements given in Table 1. ~.1 The oilseeds shall also be free from non-edible oilseeds, such as MARUA. Castor, NEEM, TARAMI.RA t Eruca sativa Mill.) and Argemone mexicana Linn.

6. PACKING
6.1 The oilseeds shall be supplied in clean, dry, sound, single, new or unmended B-twill bags in merchantable condition as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

7. MAIlKING
7.1 The bags shall be marked with the name, type and grade of the oilseeds, weight of the material, the year of the crop, and the source of supply.

8.1 Representative samples for the purpose of these tests shall be drawn in accordance with IS: 4115-1967�.

9.1 Tests shall be carried. out as prescribed in IS: 3579-1966t.
